# Mechanistically Interrogating Reversibility of the F1 Chemical–Mechanical Link

## Bottom line first

The fixed evidence establishes only one half of the chemomechanical coupling loop: chemical energy input (ATP) drives sustained directional rotation of the γ-shaft marker. The untested half is whether the coupling is reversible — whether externally imposed rotation **in the direction opposite to ATP-driven rotation** drives ATP synthesis from ADP + Pᵢ. The recommended next experiment is a magnetic-torque reversal assay on the existing surface-anchored F1 preparation, with ATP production read out directly and quantitatively by calibrated luciferase luminescence, run against a full counterfactual control matrix and a pre-registered direction convention. A clean positive result — calibrated ATP accumulation that occurs **only** under reverse rotation, scales with imposed angular velocity, and disappears in catalytically dead and torque-transmission-lacking controls — would discriminate genuine reversible coupling from the three principal confound families: ATP contamination of reagents, non-specific mechanical drift of the marker, and artifacts of the luminescent or optical readout.

---

## 1. The unresolved biological question

**Question:** Can externally imposed mechanical rotation of the F1 γ-subunit, in the direction opposite to its ATP-driven rotation, drive ATP synthesis from ADP and inorganic phosphate — i.e., is the chemomechanical coupling of isolated F1 reversible, or is it a one-way chemical-to-mechanical transducer in this preparation?

**Why the evidence packet does not answer it.** The packet states the observation "directly connects chemical fuel availability with mechanical movement" — a forward (chemical → mechanical) link only. It explicitly notes that "the supplied experiment does not directly measure ATP production during externally imposed motion or establish whether controlling one mechanical coordinate can reverse the catalytic operation." Sustained rotation in ATP is necessary but not sufficient evidence of reversibility; many motors are mechanically ratcheted and cannot be driven backward productively.

## 2. Competing mechanisms and their distinct predictions

Three classes of mechanism could explain a future observation of "ATP appeared when we rotated the bead backward":

**(M1) Reversible chemomechanical coupling.** Mechanical work imposed on γ in the reverse direction is transduced through the catalytic sites to condense ADP + Pᵢ into ATP, with approximate stoichiometry near 3 ATP per revolution (one per 120° step) and a torque × angular-distance budget consistent with the free energy of ATP synthesis under the experimental ΔG conditions.

**(M2) Contamination / basal chemistry.** ATP present as an impurity in reagents (ADP stocks, buffer, luciferase preparation) or produced by spontaneous, rotation-independent chemistry leaks into the chamber and accumulates regardless of imposed motion.

**(M3) Mechanical drift and readout artifacts.** Apparent rotation/force application is actually stage drift, bead release and Brownian motion, magnetic-field-induced heating, direct effects of the field on the luciferase reaction, or photobleaching/background drift in the luminescence signal masquerading as ATP production.

**Distinct predictions (pre-registered):**

| Condition | M1 predicts | M2 predicts | M3 predicts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reverse rotation (−) | ATP rate > 0, ∝ imposed speed (saturating) | ATP rate > 0, independent of motion | ATP "rate" correlates with field-on time, heating, or signal drift, not true γ angle |
| Forward rotation (+) | No synthesis; possibly enhanced hydrolysis (ATP *decrease* in ATP-containing buffer) | Same positive rate as reverse | Same apparent "synthesis" as reverse |
| Field on, bead absent / bead not linked | Zero | Same positive rate | Zero (no bead → no torque) or drift signal uncorrelated with steps |
| Catalytic-site-dead F1 | Zero | Same positive rate as active | Zero or artifact-level |
| No imposed rotation | Zero | Same positive rate | Baseline drift only |

The discriminating signature of M1 is the **signed interaction**: ATP accumulation above all no-motion and forward-rotation baselines, present only in the reverse condition, present only when an intact catalytic site and a physical torque-transmission path exist, and scaling with imposed angular velocity.

---

## 3. Detailed proposed protocol

### 3.1 Preparation and reaction components

- **Motor:** The existing surface-anchored F1 preparation with the fluorescent actin marker on the central γ subunit, confirmed by the packet to rotate directionally in ATP. Keep the actin–fluorophore system for imaging; add torque capability via a **streptavidin-coated paramagnetic bead** attached to the distal end of the same actin filament (or, in a parallel construct, bead attached directly via a biotinylated γ-linkage), leaving the actin visible for angular tracking.
- **Surface chemistry:** F1 anchored through a His-tag–NTA or biotin–streptavidin basal attachment; verify with ATP-driven rotation that surface anchoring does not impede rotation (matching the packet's observed behavior before torque experiments).
- **Synthesis buffer:** 50 mM HEPES or Tris (pH ~8.0), defined [Mg²⁺], [ADP] and [Pᵢ] chosen to make ADP + Pᵢ → ATP thermodynamically permissive (near-equilibrium or synthesis-favoring conditions — exact concentrations are **proposed parameters requiring empirical validation**, see §6). Include an oxygen-scavenging or antioxidant system compatible with luciferase if photodamage is a concern.
- **ATP readout:** Firefly luciferin–luciferase reagent in a separate, identical chamber geometry (side-by-side or flow-through), or in-line: luminescence calibrated against ATP standards in the same buffer. Alternatively a fluorescent ADP:ATP ratio sensor as an orthogonal check.
- **ATP scavenging:** Pre-treat all synthesis-buffer components with apyrase, then remove/heat-inactivate the apyrase, to reduce reagent ATP carryover (the primary M2 defense).

### 3.2 Manipulations

- **Imposed rotation:** Apply a rotating homogeneous magnetic field at controlled frequency (e.g., 0.1–10 Hz) to impose rotation of the bead–actin assembly. Confirm magnetic locking (bead angle tracks field phase with constant small lag) before analysis.
- **Direction set:** +1 (the ATP-hydrolysis direction defined in §3.4), −1 (opposite), and 0 (field off, or static field holding bead fixed).
- **Speed series:** Reverse-direction sweep at ≥4 angular velocities to test the predicted rate–speed relationship.
- **Duration:** Fixed 5–10 min torque episodes per chamber, with pre- and post-episode baselines.

### 3.3 Calibration

1. **Luminescence–[ATP] calibration:** ATP standard curves (≥6 points bracketing the expected range, 0.1 nM–1 µM, or appropriate) prepared in the *identical* synthesis buffer, run through the identical optical path, giving a linear fit with reported slope, intercept, and residuals. Re-run mid-experiment to track luciferase consumption.
2. **Field–torque calibration:** Characterize the bead magnetic moment and field amplitude/gradient; report the estimated applied torque. Independently estimate hydrodynamic drag from the bead–actin geometry and buffer viscosity; use the observed phase lag between field and bead angle to solve for transmitted torque. **This torque is a derived quantity requiring validation**, not a direct measurement.
3. **Rotation–angle calibration:** Pixel-to-angle calibration of the actin tracking; verify ±120° step detectability at low imposed speed.
4. **Temperature calibration:** Record chamber temperature with a micro-probe under field-on conditions to bound any magnetically induced heating (the main M3 physical artifact).
5. **Field-on-luciferase blank:** Luciferase + known [ATP] in a cell-free chamber exposed to the full field program, to verify the field does not alter luminescence output.

### 3.4 Direction convention (explicit and pre-registered)

The packet reports sustained **directional** rotation in ATP but does not name it. Therefore, define convention operationally *before the experiment*: with the F1 oriented α₃β₃-distal (stator) toward the objective and γ/actin pointing toward the viewer, record the sign of rotation during a 1 mM ATP pilot episode; designate this sign as **+1 (hydrolysis direction)** by definition. All subsequent analysis uses this signed convention. Reverse (−1) rotation is imposed only after the sign has been locked in from the pilot and documented in the analysis code. This prevents post-hoc direction assignment — the single easiest way to manufacture a false positive.

### 3.5 Counterfactual control matrix

Each row removes one necessary condition for M1; M2 and M3 predict persistence of signal in specific rows.

| # | Control | What it excludes |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Field program active, **no bead** attached | Torque-independent field effects on chemistry/luciferase (M3) |
| C2 | Bead attached, **field off** (passive) | Basal rotation-independent ATP appearance (M2), Brownian "signal" (M3) |
| C3 | **Forward (+1)** rotation | Direction insensitivity → contamination/drift (M2/M3); under M1, predicts no synthesis and, in ATP-containing buffer, hydrolysis |
| C4 | **Catalytic-site-dead F1** (e.g., a Walker-A lysine mutant or chemically blocked catalytic sites) with full reverse program | Rotation-driven synthesis requiring an intact catalytic site (M1 core claim) |
| C5 | **No ADP/Pᵢ** (synthesis substrates omitted) | Substrate-dependence; any ATP appearing here is contamination by definition (M2) |
| C6 | **Heat-denatured F1** or F1-free surface with beads | Protein-independent chemistry and bead/buffer artifacts |
| C7 | Apyrase-pre-cleared reagents vs. uncleared reagents, no rotation | Quantifies the contamination floor and the effectiveness of clearance (M2) |
| C8 | Inhibitor control (e.g., a known F1 catalytic inhibitor) under reverse rotation | Pharmacological reversibility of the coupling |
| C9 | Luciferase-free chambers imaged identically | Optical background/photobleaching drift in the ATP channel (M3) |

### 3.6 Time-resolved measurements

- **ATP channel:** Luminescence sampled continuously (≥1 Hz) from ≥2 min pre-episode through the torque episode through ≥2 min post-episode, giving within-chamber temporal dynamics rather than endpoint averages.
- **Rotation channel:** Actin/b bead imaged simultaneously or interleaved; γ angle θ(t) extracted frame-by-frame.
- **Coupled readout:** The key time-resolved test is that **d[ATP]/dt integrates with θ(t)** — under M1, ATP accumulation should begin only once reverse rotation begins, proceed at a rate locked to angular velocity, and pause when rotation pauses (run interleaved rotation episodes within one chamber to see stepwise ATP accrual tracking on/off of the field).

### 3.7 Replication and analysis

- **Biological replication:** ≥3 independent F1 preparations; **technical replication:** ≥20 chambers (or ≥50 individually tracked molecules, if single-molecule fluorescence ATP sensing is used) per condition.
- **Randomization and blinding:** Condition order randomized within each preparation day; the analyst given direction-coded data under blinded labels until the analysis pipeline is frozen.
- **Primary analysis:** Per-chamber ATP accumulation slope during the torque episode minus the pre-episode baseline drift, converted to ATP via the calibration curve. Mixed-effects model with fixed effects of direction (±1), speed, control status, and their interactions, and random intercepts for preparation day and chamber. Pre-registered primary contrast: **reverse vs. forward slope difference**, and reverse vs. C2 (field-off) difference.
- **Secondary analyses:** ATP rate vs. imposed angular velocity (linearity and saturation); per-molecule power output (torque × ω) compared with the inferred ATP free-energy cost; fraction of chambers showing any signal.
- **Multiplicity/robustness:** Report all conditions regardless of outcome (no condition dropping); sensitivity analysis excluding borderline chambers.

---

## 4. How the complete result pattern discriminates the mechanisms

**Pattern A — M1 (reversible coupling) confirmed:** ATP accumulates above baseline **only** in C-reverse with intact F1, bead-linked torque, and ADP+Pᵢ present. The signal is (i) absent in forward rotation, field-off, bead-absent, dead-F1, and no-substrate conditions; (ii) time-locked to the rotation episode; (iii) monotonically related to imposed angular velocity; (iv) abolished by F1 inhibitor; and (v) of magnitude consistent with torque × revolutions divided by the ATP synthesis free energy (within an order of magnitude, given parameter uncertainty). Contamination (M2) cannot produce direction-dependence or substrate-dependence; drift/artifacts (M3) cannot produce catalytic-site-dependence or field-off suppression combined with bead-dependence.

**Pattern B — M2 (contamination):** ATP appears at the same rate in reverse, forward, field-off, bead-absent, dead-F1, and no-substrate conditions — any condition where reagents are present. Discriminated by uniformity across the matrix and persistence in C5/C7.

**Pattern C — M3a (mechanical drift):** Apparent rotation occurs but the angle signal lacks the ±120° step structure, or ATP "production" appears in the bead-absent condition or correlates with field-on duration rather than tracked angle. Discriminated by requiring angle–luciferase temporal correlation *and* the C1 control.

**Pattern D — M3b (readout artifact):** Luciferase response varies with field exposure (seen in the cell-free field blank, §3.3.5), or luminescence drifts identically in luciferase-free/light-exposed control chambers (C9), or chamber heating under field correlates with the signal. Discriminated by the physical controls and the requirement that apparent ATP be substrate-dependent.

**Ambiguous middle cases** must be pre-committed in interpretation: e.g., ATP in reverse but *also* in forward rotation (suggests partial contamination riding on real coupling, resolvable by isotope-based ATP quantification or tighter apyrase clearing); or reverse-direction ATP under field that persists with dead F1 (torque pathway artifact, not coupling).

---

## 5. Conditional conclusions (pre-registered)

- **Positive:** Reverse-direction, substrate-dependent, catalytic-site-dependent, bead-dependent ATP accumulation at rates consistent with coupling stoichiometry → supports reversible chemomechanical coupling in isolated F1; next step is torque–ATP stoichiometry measurement.
- **Negative:** No ATP above contamination floor under any imposed condition, despite verified magnetic locking and torque transmission → F1 in this surface-anchored preparation does not support productive reversal under these conditions; does not exclude reversibility in F₀F₁ or under different ΔG conditions.
- **Ambiguous:** Direction-insensitive ATP appearance → resubmit to the control matrix with improved reagent clearance; only a signed, matrix-clean signal advances the mechanistic claim.

## 6. Measured values vs. parameters requiring validation

**Directly measured:** actin/bead angle trajectories θ(t); field frequency and phase; luminescence intensity; calibration-curve counts; chamber temperature; rotation rate of markers.

**Derived or assumed parameters that require independent validation before quantitative claims:** (i) the torque actually transmitted to γ (depends on bead moment, linkage compliance, and phase lag — must be validated by drag-based calibration and, ideally, by comparison with known F1 load behavior); (ii) buffer [ADP], [Pᵢ], [Mg²⁺], and the effective free energy ΔG of ATP synthesis under chamber conditions; (iii) the fraction of surface-anchored F1 that is active and torque-coupled; (iv) the luciferase response in the exact synthesis buffer; (v) the assumed ~3 ATP/rev stoichiometry used only for the consistency check, not as an input. None of these are established by the evidence packet, and no results described here have been observed — the entire protocol and its predictions are proposed.

**Key consequential uncertainties that could change the recommendation:** if the paramagnetic bead cannot be coupled to the existing actin–γ construct without killing rotation (pilot failure), the design shifts to electrorotation or an optical-tweezer handle; if reverse rotation mechanically disconnects the actin from γ, angle tracking must verify torque transmission continuously, otherwise all negative results are uninterpretable.
